artboards.title: A — the same window, one step down
B — two columns, the result gets the room
C — the rule is one band, the note is the window
What we have now, for scale

annotations.text:
Same kit, one step tighter — nothing here is a new component.
Controls 42 → 34 (the kit's own size s). Rows 40 → 34 (the kit's minimal sidebar). Text 16 → 14. Badges 28 → 22. Gaps 12 → 8. Window 1040 → 900.
Pills, fills, accent wash, the lifted block and the soft shadows all stay exactly as they are.
A — the stack you already have, only denser. Delete became an icon so the head holds one line. Least risk, least change.
B — a desktop has width, so match and rule sit side by side and the result takes the whole row underneath. The preview finally shows more than three lines.
C — the whole rule collapses into one band and the rest of the window is the note. Fewest boxes, most preview; the numbered stages go away, which is the thing to argue about.
Three ways to show the turn from text to widget without a box inside a box. A is in the Live frame now.
